text: Eight lessons expanded to full depth: the deal clock, the voucher rule, what QAPs reward (with a new pick-your-state finder for each state's credit agency), who owns the deal, utility allowances, the deal team, the development budget and income averaging. Each adds worked examples with made-up numbers, the rules with citations, how it works in practice, and common myths.
New home: this site is now lihtcexplained.com. Old vankyleproperties.com links forward here. Social handles are now @lihtcexplained. LIHTC Explained is a VanKyle Properties publication.
New page: income and rent limits in your county, a quick lookup using HUD's FY2026 MTSP limits.

Module 2 (Sizing the credit) lessons expanded to full depth: worked examples, the first-year credit rule, how QCT/DDA maps are drawn, a sorted sample budget, a sample equity pay-in schedule, nonprofit qualification, and how credit and bond caps are built and handed out.

IRS released 2027 amounts (Rev. Proc. 2026-35): housing credit ceiling of $3.53 per resident or $4,082,400 minimum; private activity bond cap of $135 per resident or $410,520,000 minimum; rehab minimum of $9,000 per low-income unit.
HUD announced the 2027 Qualified Census Tracts and Difficult Development Areas (basis boost map).
HUD began winding down RAD Restore-Rebuild (formerly Faircloth-to-RAD) for new requests.
HUD's FY2026 income limits took effect, with a 45-day grace period. Increases were capped at 10%; the average change was about 3.4%.

The permanent 12% increase in 9% credit allocations began ($3.416 per resident for 2026). The 25% bond test began for buildings placed in service after 2025 with at least 5% of building and land cost financed by bonds issued after 2025.
Public Law 119-21 was signed. A proposed 30% basis boost for rural and tribal areas was not included in the final law.
